subject: maths
question: An agent sells a pressure cooker with a marked price of ₹8,460 at a discount of 30%. What is the selling price (in ₹) of the pressure cooker?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Discount = 30% ⇒ Customer pays 70% of marked price

⇒ Selling Price = 70% of 8460

⇒ 8460 × 0.7 = 5922

**∴ Answer = 5922**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marked Price = 8460, Discount = 30%

**Formula used:**

Selling Price = Marked Price − Discount

**Calculation:**

⇒ Discount = 30% of 8460 = (30 ÷ 100) × 8460

⇒ Discount = 2538

⇒ Selling Price = 8460 − 2538

⇒ Selling Price = 5922

**∴ The correct answer is 5922.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Discount Concept

Discount = Marked Price × (Discount% ÷ 100)

Selling Price Shortcut

Selling Price = Marked Price × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100

Successive Discount

If multiple discounts apply: Final Price = MP × (1 − d1) × (1 − d2)
